title: Solutions and Solubility
summary: Solute + solvent = solution. How much can dissolve, what makes it dissolve faster, and how to read a solubility curve.

ib.note: Strong Criterion C opportunity: collecting data and drawing a solubility curve

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 9: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents and Solutions
Ch 2: Is Matter Around Us Pure?, section 2.2 (solutions, concentration)

objectives: I can use the words solute, solvent, solution, soluble and insoluble correctly.
I can explain what saturated and unsaturated solutions are.
I can collect data to draw a solubility curve and use it to make predictions.
I can calculate the concentration of a solution.
I can explain why mass is conserved when a substance dissolves.
misconceptions: Dissolving is the same as melting.
When sugar dissolves it disappears, so the mass goes down.
Stirring lets you dissolve an unlimited amount.
All solids dissolve better in hot water by the same amount.
